subject: Request: Temporary rate alignment & one-off credit for Vision API migration delay
messages:
From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@farsight.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Vision migration: increased costs and timeline impact

Hi Lauren —

Quick note from our side: the Vision API migration to the new embedding model pushed our rollout by ~3 weeks. During that time we had to fall back to the older, more expensive runtime and traffic spiked during testing. We will absorb some costs, but this is hitting our Q2 spend unexpectedly.

Is there any temporary pricing accommodation or a credit you can offer while we finish the rollout? I can share usage reports. We really want to stay with Redwood long term but this timing gap is painful.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Ellis
Head of Platform, Farsight

Attachment: Farsight_usage_q2.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Vision migration: increased costs and timeline impact

Aditya / Karthik — forwarding Sarah's ask. TL;DR: Farsight had to run on the legacy Vision runtime for ~3 weeks and their Q2 invoice will be materially higher. They want either a temporary rate alignment (discount for the fallback window) or a one-off credit to offset the overage.

Context: Farsight is a mid-market account, committed to Dedicated v2. They are a high-signal reference for vision/embedding latency work. Product tells me the migration slip was due to a GPU kernel regression we patched but it required model pinning for customers during the rollout windows.

Proposed options (to escalate):
- small one-off credit to cover the delta for the fallback period (suggested $15k based on usage)
- temporary effective rate alignment for June invoice only (apply discounted unit rate retroactively for the 3-week window)

Need decision + an exec sign-off path if > $10k. Karthik, can you advise on precedence and whether we can offer a retroactive temporary rate? Aditya, please weigh in on exec escalation.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — I reviewed the usage CSV (thanks Sarah for sending) and the delta looks like ~18% higher token-equivalent cost for the fallback period. Precedence: we have done both credits and retroactive rate adjustments before, but typically anything above $10k needs an Exec OK and Finance sign-off.

Questions for product: can we reliably say this was due to our migration patch and not a customer-side misconfiguration? If product confirms, I support a targeted make-whole (credit) tied to the exact fallback dates. Credits are easier for Finance to reconcile.

Marissa, can you estimate the margin impact if we do a $15k credit vs. a 30-day temporary rate alignment? Also, if we attach a short ROE (mutual action plan) that commits Farsight to the next 2 quarters of usage / feature adoption, we can treat as commercial remediation + commitment.

Karthik
Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy

All — my rough back-of-envelope shows a $13k credit covers the exact delta for the fallback window; a temporary rate adjustment that applies retroactively would be slightly more complex for billing but in the same ballpark (maybe $14–16k depending on rounding and overage tiers).

I recommend the one-off credit tied to dates: simple, auditable, and sufficient to keep the customer happy. If we get a 2-quarter commitment (standard SOW addendum) we can classify it as a commercial concession with renewal incentives.

I can run the finance approval flow if we lock the amount and language. Per policy, anything > $10k needs an Exec email sign-off (CRO or CEO) — I can start the DocuSign if you confirm amount.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
